The proposed locally uniform tail control is valid. With K_R=||grad V(0)||+R/eta, one may take A_R=|V(0)|+K_R^2/c: Taylor's lower bound and K_R r <= c r^2/4+K_R^2/c give W_y(x)>=c||x||^2/4-A_R on ||y||<=R. This bounds exp(-W_y), every polynomial position moment, and the first two y derivatives by integrable polynomial-Gaussian envelopes independent of y in the ball. Positivity and continuity on a ball of positive Lebesgue volume give a strictly positive normalizer, not merely nonnegativity.

The first derivative multiplier (x_i-y_i)/eta and second derivative multiplier (x_i-y_i)(x_j-y_j)/eta^2-delta_ij/eta have the stated signs. Their locally uniform domination and pointwise continuity justify continuous parameter differentiation twice. Consequently q_eta is genuinely positive C2 and U_eta=-log q_eta is C2 without assuming an integrable prior.

Normalizing exp(-W_y) gives a probability posterior with vector position in L2. Directly differentiating q_eta and using -D2 log q=(Dq tensor Dq)/q^2-D2q/q yields grad U_eta=(y-E X)/eta and Hess U_eta=I/eta-Cov(X)/eta^2. This reasoning does not assume either the prior probability law or a covariance identity as an input.

The two reusable covariance inequalities have different directions and both are necessary: b^(-1)I <= Cov <= c^(-1)I. Multiplication by -eta^(-2) reverses their order. The identities eta^(-1)-eta^(-2)/c=m/(1+m eta) and eta^(-1)-eta^(-2)/b=M/(1+M eta) verify the exact signed Hessian endpoints. The scalar map t/(1+t eta) is increasing on t>-1/eta. Quadratic potentials with curvature m or M attain the corresponding endpoint, so the universal endpoints are sharp.

Since the actual Hessian is self-adjoint, its operator norm is bounded by the maximum of the absolute values of the two signed endpoints. Integrating D grad U_eta along a segment proves the claimed nonnegative global Lipschitz constant. The reduction to M/(1+M eta) is valid when m>=0; an upper Loewner bound alone is insufficient in the signed case.

For V(x)=-a||x||^2/2 and 0<eta<1/a, completing the square gives q_eta(y)=(1-a eta)^(-d/2) exp(a||y||^2/[2(1-a eta)]). Thus U_eta=(d/2)log(1-a eta)-a||y||^2/[2(1-a eta)], Hess U_eta=-aI/(1-a eta), and the exact gradient Lipschitz constant is a/(1-a eta)>0. The proposed M/(1+M eta) is negative. Tonelli applies to the nonnegative measurable joint kernel and the Gaussian kernel has unit integral, so the equality of total masses is valid as an extended nonnegative integral. Both masses diverge in the concave-quadratic example despite finite positive q_eta at every point.
